one_line: A shared decision room where humans and agents collaborate, but only a human can close the decision.
what_it_does: Portable rooms expose role-specific tools for proposals, evidence, challenges, briefs, and tasks, with a human-only final stamp.
leverage_rationale: Shared mutable state, role-specific tool registration, and an intentionally absent Decide tool make WebMCP central rather than cosmetic.
leverage_evidence: Same room object for multiple agents and people
Human-only Stamp Decide and immutable Decisions Wall
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent end-to-end room workflow and live sync kernel; the frame-sheet evidence is present, though no transcript is supplied.
impact_rationale: Teams needing auditable human-agent decisions have a concrete use case and clear safety boundary.
creativity_rationale: Portable shared artifact plus deliberate human/agent role split is a memorable WebMCP-native interaction.
creativity_evidence: Claude and ChatGPT can work the same object
Decide is not registered as a tool
usability_note: Clear primary workflow; usability appears strong from the described shared surface and demo packaging.
standouts: Human-only close is a strong governance pattern
advance_reason: Strong concept and sufficient packet evidence; advance.

one_line: An accessible clinic booking page whose agent finds and holds slots while the person makes the booking decision.
what_it_does: The agent searches cancellation waves and holds appointments; the page offers voice, switch, gesture, and scanning-keyboard inputs for the final human choices.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives an accessibility-focused agent structured booking state and safe holds while preserving a human booking boundary.
leverage_evidence: Human confirmation via multiple input modes
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is unusually complete and the video packet is authoritative, but transcript-free evidence limits certainty on every edge case.
impact_rationale: It addresses a specific, underserved audience facing real booking friction with a purpose-built interaction model.
impact_evidence: People using switch, head-pointer, voice, or gesture access
creativity_rationale: Combines agent assistance with inclusive multimodal human control in a way that is both socially meaningful and technically ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Agent asks on page instead of separate window
usability_note: Clear primary workflow; usability appears strong from the described shared surface and demo packaging.
advance_reason: Strong concept and sufficient packet evidence; advance.

one_line: A bounded delegate agent that handles approved decisions during a person’s absence and escalates the rest.
what_it_does: Users prepare a live policy/configuration for a delegate; WebMCP tools change with identity and state so the agent can act only inside approved boundaries.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic, browser-computed tool surfaces enforce delegation boundaries in shared state; this is substantially beyond generic UI automation.
execution_rationale: The concept and described controls are strong, with a live demo packet, but execution claims are partly description-led without transcript.
impact_rationale: People facing planned or sudden absence have a concrete need for bounded continuity across work and personal logistics.
impact_evidence: Hospital stay, custody handoff, contractor coverage
creativity_rationale: The “absence has a shape” framing and policy-governed stand-in is an original, ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent acts only on what user would approve
usability_note: Clear primary workflow; usability appears strong from the described shared surface and demo packaging.
standouts: Useful across planned and unplanned absence
advance_reason: Strong concept and sufficient packet evidence; advance.

one_line: A tracker that detects stale job applications and invoices and lets an agent follow up.
what_it_does: Two tracker tabs expose structured records, status transitions, stale detection, reminders, summaries, and leverage opportunities.
leverage_rationale: A live mutable record plus batch stale-state operations are meaningfully better than an agent scraping a passive tracker, though generic automation could approximate parts.
execution_rationale: The scope is clearly specified and the workflow appears complete for a focused tracker; evidence is video-backed but transcript-free.
impact_rationale: Job seekers and freelancers have a specific recurring problem and the product automates tedious tracking and follow-up timing.
creativity_rationale: The unification of job and invoice “ghosting” is a sharp conceptual angle with useful agent actions, though the category itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Same mechanic across employment and freelance work
usability_note: Clear primary workflow; usability appears strong from the described shared surface and demo packaging.
advance_reason: Strong concept and sufficient packet evidence; advance.

one_line: A shoe shop with identical human and agent surfaces, including a no-tools control route.
what_it_does: The agent can search, compare, inspect stock, shortlist, and stage a bag in shared catalog state; a parallel no-tools route tests the WebMCP delta.
leverage_rationale: The controlled tools/no-tools comparison directly tests whether structured live-tab state beats scraping, especially for stock, size, bag, and prompt-injection resistance.
leverage_evidence: Shared bag and staged, non-purchasing checkout
execution_rationale: The packet describes a well-scoped, safety-conscious demo with explicit purchase prevention and a comparative control; frame-sheet inspection was unavailable due to vision rate limiting.
execution_evidence: Keep and stage then Review and confirm
impact_rationale: Shopping is a real multi-step stateful task and the product demonstrates a credible niche value: safer, more precise agent shopping without accidental purchase.
creativity_rationale: The two-door experimental design and explicit counterfactual route make the WebMCP claim unusually testable and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Same catalog with and without tools
usability_note: Clear primary workflow; usability appears strong from the described shared surface and demo packaging.
red_flags: Vision service rate-limited during review; score confidence reduced
advance_reason: Strong concept and sufficient packet evidence; advance.

one_line: A site-native issue-reporting tool that lets agents submit structured failures with bounded telemetry evidence.
what_it_does: TinCan adds report_site_issue to WebMCP, collecting category, severity, expected/observed behavior, and privacy-preserving OpenTelemetry-compatible evidence.
leverage_rationale: A structured reporting channel closes a real gap between agent actions and site observability; it is more reliable than a free-form support ticket.
execution_rationale: The product is narrowly scoped and technically coherent, though the central demo appears to showcase one tool rather than a broad workflow.
impact_rationale: Every agent-driven website can generate silent or ambiguous failures; site owners and users both benefit from precise reports.
impact_evidence: No screenshots, credentials, DOM, or keystrokes captured
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP as an observability/reporting plane is a fresh infrastructure angle with a disciplined privacy model.
creativity_evidence: Agent reports directly to the site it used
usability_note: Clear primary workflow; usability appears strong from the described shared surface and demo packaging.
advance_reason: Strong concept and sufficient packet evidence; advance.

impact_rationale: Crisis-response learners and strategy players get a compelling, concrete simulation that teaches reasoning under pressure rather than button clicking.
impact_evidence: Dependencies across power, data, water, roads, emergency response
creativity_rationale: Ambitious, memorable, and deeply aligned with WebMCP: a real-time crisis room where agent reasoning and human accountability are gameplay.

advance_reason: Strong concept and sufficient packet evidence; advance.

Person and agent edit the same dashboard
